stages.prompt: Read the item, its fence, and the design documents under docs/ that the change reaches. When the request's words amend or overturn a decision recorded in a design document's ledger, do not write do-it-now or a proposal: end your report with OBSTACLE: definition, CRITERIA: <criteria>, EVIDENCE: <the design document, the recorded decision in its ledger, and how the request amends or overturns it>, and RESULT: blocked so the item goes to the design seat to update the document before any build. Otherwise, when the request is small and clear (one coherent change within the fence, no split into pieces, no question for the owner), your first move may be to decide 'do it now': record that choice in the do-it-now file in your output directory, make the change, test it, commit once on this lane, write no proposal, and end with RESULT: done. Otherwise, do not write or commit repository files: to divide the work, write the optional proposal output targeting work with workflow build-pieces@v1 and args.pieces, a list of at most 12 objects in execution order. Each object has id, seat, access (read_only or write), prompt, optional outputs mapping names to types, and for write access a nonempty write_scope within the item's fence. Read-only pieces must omit write_scope. Choose seats mapped by policy and do not assign writes to read-only seats. If no division is useful, propose nothing. When a piece cannot be cut without a design decision, write no proposal and end your report with OBSTACLE: owner, a QUESTION: line containing the one specific question, and RESULT: blocked.

Read the criteria, joined candidate diff and the producers' outputs. For each criterion marked done, name the satisfying piece as node:<id> in evidence. For each criterion no piece covers, mark it not-done with a reason beginning uncovered:. A not-done finding, including an uncovered: one, goes to the build step on the candidate you read, with your findings word for word; write reasons the builder can act on. Only when a finding says the plan itself is wrong (the pieces or their scopes cannot meet the criterion), begin that criterion's not-done reason with plan-wrong: and the item returns to plan instead. The build step may also return the item to plan by ending blocked with an obstacle of kind definition whose EVIDENCE begins plan-wrong:. The gate and judge still decide landing.
